anchor.statement: Lemma 7.1. For the labels and phases in Equations (6.8), (7.2) and (7.3), there exists a sufficiently small q ∗ > 0, common to all labels and fixed derivative orders, such that every rectangle on 0 < q < q ∗ has the following properties. Every e ikm Φ , m ∈ Z \ {0}, is single-valued in θ , with nonzero angular frequency. On the rectangle 0 ≤ v ≤ L s , |n Φ − B s (s(v), K)| + |n ′ Φ | ≤ C/S ∗ , E ik := (t ∗ + bD r + F ∂ θ + GD z ) Φ = O( ε S C ∗ ). (7.9) The estimate for E ik in (7.9) holds in every fixed coefficient derivative, with a corresponding polynomial degree. The coefficients extend smoothly to the fixed enlargement. All fixed mixed derivatives in the slow, transverse, and pulse coordinates of n Φ , and of the frames used here, have polynomial bounds in S ∗ . The real 3 × 2 matrix B in (7.8) has columns forming a basis of n ⊥ Φ , and is also viewed as a map C2 −→ {t ∈ C3 : n Φ · t = 0 }. It has a uniformly bounded left inverse Bℓ and satisfies B ℓ (A Φ B − B ′ ) = diag( λ , − λ ) + E, λ (v) = λ 0 √︁ 1 + s(v) 2 , |E| ≤ C/S ∗ . (7.10) For the damping coefficient d in (7.5), put d ref = ε k 2 B 2 s (1 + s 2 ). Then |d − d ref | ≤ C/S ∗ . (7.11)

correspondence.note: The phase-normal comparison, the four modal errors |E_ab| ≤ C/S∗ about diag(λ, −λ), and |d − d_ref| ≤ C/S∗ hold under one band threshold common to all labels, with (7.10) stated as bounds on scalar modal coefficients rather than through a named left inverse B^ℓ. Not stated in these declarations: E_ik = O(εS∗^C), single-valuedness of e^{ikmΦ}, and the polynomial bounds on mixed derivatives.

links.doc:
The actual phase family satisfies every order-zero input of the
previous primary-pulse theorem.  Its normal comparison, modal errors,
and damping comparison are proved here from the base and mesh data.
